caption:
Manganese doesn't get much attention, but it's a cofactor your body needs to activate enzymes that build connective tissue and keep bones strong from the inside out. Copper works quietly alongside iron — without enough of it, iron can't actually be transported into your red blood cells, so you can eat plenty of iron-rich food and still feel drained if copper is low. And selenium is one of the few minerals your thyroid gland uses directly to convert thyroid hormone into its active form, which is a big reason why just two Brazil nuts a day can make a noticeable difference. Everyone's body is different, so adjust based on what works for you.
